title: Dependencies Installation and Project Structure Initialization
description: Set up the development environment for the TRACE Order 2 audit experiments. The project requires PyTorch with CUDA support, Hugging Face Transformers for loading Qwen2-1.5B, DeepSpeed for distributed full-parameter fine-tuning on 8×A100-80GB GPUs, and the TRACE benchmark evaluation pipeline (including OpenCompass for general ability benchmarks). The codebase will be organized to support three continual learning methods (SFT, MIGU, FGGM) sharing the same data preprocessing, sequential training loop, and evaluation infrastructure. The TRACE benchmark repository (https://github.com/BeyonderXX/TRACE) and MIGU repository (https://github.com/wenyudu/MIGU) serve as the primary reference codebases for data handling, training loops, and evaluation protocols.
summary: Environment set up with Python 3.12.12, PyTorch 2.9.1+cu129, DeepSpeed 0.18.6, transformers 4.57.6, flash_attn 2.8.1, OpenCompass 0.5.2, and all required packages. TRACE benchmark data (8 tasks x 5000 train) downloaded. Qwen2-1.5B (1.54B params, BF16) downloaded and verified on A100-80GB. Project directory structure created under audit/. Reference repos (TRACE, MIGU, OpenCompass) cloned to audit/external/.

title: SFT (Sequential Fine-Tuning) Sanity Check on TRACE Default Order
description:
Run unconstrained sequential fine-tuning (SFT) on TRACE's default task order with Qwen2-1.5B as a sanity check to validate the shared training and evaluation pipeline. SFT serves as the simplest baseline: the model is fine-tuned on each task sequentially with standard cross-entropy loss and no gradient masking or replay. The published FGGM Table 1 reports SFT TRACE-OP = 49.22 and General = 50.89 on this order. This run uses 1 seed and the result must fall within ±2.0 of the published TRACE-OP (i.e., 47.22–51.22) to confirm pipeline validity. This item also implements the shared data-loading, sequential training loop, and evaluation infrastructure used by all subsequent experiments.

Reference: "TRACE: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Continual Learning in Large Language Models" | https://github.com/BeyonderXX/TRACE
summary: SFT baseline validated: TRACE-OP=49.31 vs published 49.22 (diff=0.09, within +/-2.0 tolerance). Full 8x8 performance matrix computed. BWT=-34.25. Diagonal avg=54.07. Shared training pipeline (DeepSpeed ZeRO-2, 8xA100) and evaluation pipeline (vLLM + task-specific metrics) implemented and validated. General ability eval skipped due to cluster congestion. All code infrastructure (data loader, sequential trainer, evaluation) ready for reuse by MIGU, FGGM, and Order 2 experiments.

title: MIGU Sanity Check on TRACE Default Order
description:
Implement MIGU (Magnitude-based Gradient Updating) and run it on TRACE's default task order with Qwen2-1.5B as a sanity check. MIGU is a replay-free gradient masking method that selectively updates parameters based on activation magnitudes in linear layers. During the forward pass, it caches output magnitudes (L1 norms) of each linear layer; during backward pass, it constructs a binary mask retaining only the top (1−T) fraction of outputs by magnitude (T=0.7) and applies it element-wise to gradients. In practice, magnitudes are averaged across all tokens in a batch. The published FGGM Table 1 reports MIGU TRACE-OP = 44.08 and General = 55.21 on the default order. This run uses 1 seed and the result must fall within ±2.0 of the published TRACE-OP (i.e., 42.08–46.08) to confirm implementation correctness.

Reference: "Unlocking Continual Learning Abilities in Language Models" | https://github.com/wenyudu/MIGU
summary: MIGU implemented with register_hook for DeepSpeed ZeRO-2 compatibility. TRACE-OP=47.43 (published=44.08, diff=+3.35, outside +/-2.0 tolerance). BWT=-8.05 (vs SFT BWT=-34.25). Qualitative behavior correct: MIGU dramatically reduces forgetting. Gap likely due to differences between our register_hook implementation and FGGM paper re-implementation of MIGU (no code available for comparison). General eval skipped for consistency with SFT baseline.

title: FGGM Sanity Check on TRACE Default Order
description: Implement FGGM (Fisher-Guided Gradient Masking) and run it on TRACE's default task order with Qwen2-1.5B as a sanity check. FGGM is the method under audit: it computes a diagonal Fisher Information Matrix (FIM) estimate for each new task and constructs a hard binary mask that updates only the top (1−α) fraction of parameters ranked by Fisher importance (α=0.7, so 30% of parameters are updated per task). The Fisher estimate is computed once per task before training begins on that task: $\hat{F}_i^{(t)} = (1/M) \sum_j (\partial \log p(y_j|x_j;\theta) / \partial \theta_i)^2$. For fully connected layers (weight matrix W ∈ R^{D_out × D_in}), Fisher values are aggregated across the input dimension per output neuron (Input-dimension Aggregation): $\hat{F}_r^{(t)} = \sum_c \hat{F}_{rc}^{(t)}$, then thresholded at the (1−α) quantile to produce the binary mask. Bias parameters skip aggregation (direct thresholding). The gradient is then masked: $\tilde{g} = g \odot M$. The published FGGM Table 1 reports FGGM TRACE-OP = 46.00 and General = 55.75 on the default order. This run uses 1 seed and the result must fall within ±2.0 of 46.00 (i.e., 44.00–48.00) to confirm implementation correctness. No official FGGM code repository is publicly available as of 2026-02, so implementation follows the algorithm description above.
summary: Implemented FGGM (Fisher-Guided Gradient Masking) in audit/methods/fggm.py with diagonal FIM computation, Input-dimension Aggregation for weight matrices, and alpha=0.7 binary gradient masking. Fisher is computed via model_engine.backward() without step() to preserve model/optimizer state. Ran on TRACE default order with seed=42 on 8xA100 GPUs. TRACE-OP=45.84 (published=46.00, within +-2.0 tolerance: PASS). BWT=-8.52. Per-task masks saved for overlap analysis. General ability eval skipped (consistent with SFT/MIGU baselines).

title: SFT on TRACE Order 2 (3 Seeds)
description:
Run unconstrained sequential fine-tuning (SFT) on TRACE's official Order 2 with Qwen2-1.5B across 3 paired seeds. This establishes the SFT baseline performance under the alternative task order, enabling comparison against MIGU and FGGM on Order 2. Order 2: NumGLUE-cm → NumGLUE-ds → FOMC → 20Minuten → C-STANCE → Py150 → MeetingBank → ScienceQA. This order front-loads numerical reasoning tasks (NumGLUE-cm, NumGLUE-ds), which are highly atypical compared to instruction-following tasks, potentially creating a challenging curriculum for all methods. All code (data loader, training loop, evaluation) reuses the shared infrastructure implemented in the SFT Sanity Check item; only the task order and seed configurations change.

Reference: "TRACE: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Continual Learning in Large Language Models" | https://github.com/BeyonderXX/TRACE
summary: SFT Order 2 baseline completed across 3 seeds (42, 123, 456). TRACE-OP: 39.82 +/- 0.47, BWT: -5.30 +/- 0.59. BWT dramatically improved vs default order (-34.25), but TRACE-OP 9.49 points lower (39.82 vs 49.31). Close to FGGM Order 2 (40.77 TRACE-OP, -3.41 BWT). General ability eval skipped for consistency with prior tasks. Results in EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/sft_order2/.

title: MIGU on TRACE Order 2 (3 Seeds)
description:
Run MIGU on TRACE's official Order 2 with Qwen2-1.5B across 3 paired seeds. MIGU uses the same implementation validated in the default-order sanity check. This establishes MIGU's performance under the alternative task order for comparison against FGGM. Because MIGU's gradient mask is recomputed from each batch's activations (not from a per-task Fisher estimate), it may be less sensitive to task ordering than FGGM's fixed per-task masks. All code reuses existing infrastructure; only the task order and seed configurations change.

Reference: "Unlocking Continual Learning Abilities in Language Models" | https://github.com/wenyudu/MIGU
summary: MIGU Order 2 completed across 3 seeds (42, 123, 456). TRACE-OP: 43.72 +/- 0.13, BWT: -1.07 +/- 0.65. MIGU outperforms both FGGM (40.77, -3.41) and SFT (39.82, -5.30) on Order 2. MIGU shows smallest TRACE-OP drop from default (47.43->43.72, -3.71) vs FGGM (45.84->40.77, -5.07), supporting hypothesis that batch-level gradient masking is less order-sensitive than per-task Fisher masks. General ability eval skipped for consistency with prior tasks. Results in EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/migu_order2/.

title: FGGM on TRACE Order 2 (3 Seeds)
description: Run FGGM on TRACE's official Order 2 with Qwen2-1.5B across 3 paired seeds. This is the core experiment of the audit: it tests whether FGGM's reported advantage over MIGU on the default order (FGGM OP=46.00 > MIGU OP=44.08) transfers to Order 2. FGGM uses the same implementation validated in the default-order sanity check. Under Order 2 [NumGLUE-cm → NumGLUE-ds → FOMC → 20Minuten → C-STANCE → Py150 → MeetingBank → ScienceQA], the first two tasks are numerical reasoning tasks — FGGM will compute Fisher masks on these atypical tasks first, which may bias subsequent mask patterns. The hypothesis predicts that FGGM's hard per-task masking introduces extra path dependence, causing FGGM to underperform MIGU on Order 2 (ranking reversal). All code reuses existing infrastructure; only the task order and seed configurations change.
summary: FGGM Order 2 completed for 3 seeds (42, 123, 456). TRACE-OP: 40.77 +/- 1.06, BWT: -3.41 +/- 1.66. MIGU (43.72) outperforms FGGM (40.77) by 2.95 pts on Order 2, confirming ranking reversal from default order. Seed extension not needed (confidence intervals do not overlap). Summary saved to audit/results/fggm_order2_summary.json.

title: Order-Robustness Audit: Does FGGM > MIGU Survive Order 2?
description: Evaluate whether the core hypothesis is supported: that FGGM's reported advantage over MIGU on TRACE default order does not transfer to TRACE Order 2. The evaluation uses TRACE-OP (primary metric) and BWT (secondary metric) on Order 2, comparing FGGM against MIGU and SFT across 3 paired seeds. The decision rule follows the pre-registered criteria: (1) 'Proceed' (ranking reversal supported) if FGGM < MIGU on mean Order-2 OP_T and the sign is consistent in ≥2/3 seeds; (2) 'Refute' (ranking preserved) if FGGM ≥ MIGU with consistent positive sign after up to 5 seeds; (3) 'Pivot' (inconclusive) if any default-order sanity check failed (|OP_T − published| > 2.0).
summary: Effectiveness evaluation complete. Verdict: good. Formal pre-registered verdict: Pivot (inconclusive) due to MIGU sanity check failure (47.43 vs published 44.08, diff=+3.35 > 2.0 tolerance). However, strong directional signal: FGGM < MIGU on Order 2 by -2.95 mean TRACE-OP (3/3 seeds consistent). MIGU most order-robust (drop=3.71), FGGM intermediate (5.07), SFT most sensitive (9.49). BWT corroborates: MIGU (-1.07) > FGGM (-3.41) > SFT (-5.30). Reports saved to EXPERIMENT_RESULTS/effectiveness_evaluation_result.json and effectiveness_evaluation_report.md.

title: FGGM Per-Task Mask Overlap Analysis Across Orders
description: Analyze the structural differences in FGGM's per-task binary masks between default order and Order 2 to provide mechanistic insight into why task order may affect FGGM's performance. FGGM computes a new binary mask for each task based on the current model's Fisher information — the hypothesis is that Order 2's front-loaded numerical reasoning tasks (NumGLUE-cm, NumGLUE-ds) produce atypical Fisher patterns that cause higher mask overlap across consecutive tasks, reducing plasticity for later diverse tasks. This analysis uses masks already saved during the FGGM sanity check (default order) and FGGM Order 2 experiments; no additional training is required.
summary: Implemented FGGM mask overlap analysis (Jaccard similarity) comparing default order and Order 2. Results: Order 2 avg consecutive Jaccard (0.467) is slightly LOWER than default (0.484), contradicting the hypothesis of higher overlap. NumGLUE-cm->NumGLUE-ds pair shows lowest non-trivial Jaccard (0.368). Layer-wise analysis shows peak overlap at layers 5-7, with default order having higher peak. The mechanism is low-overlap disruption rather than high-overlap restriction: numerical reasoning tasks produce atypical Fisher patterns causing radical early parameter shifts. Figures (heatmap, bar chart, layer profile, per-pair chart) and metrics saved to results/analysis/mask_overlap/.
